Scottsdale Golf Transportation: Rates, Seats and Bag Planning

Scottsdale Sprinters runs Scottsdale and Phoenix golf days in chauffeured Executive Sprinters first — the Executive Black Sprinter and the Executive White Sprinter, 14 seats each — and moves larger golf groups and tournament fields in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) or the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. A 4-hour morning starts at $580 in the Executive Black Sprinter at $145 an hour; an 8-hour day is $1,015, because 8 requested hours earn 1 free hour on the published ladder. The 14-passenger Sprinters hold about 30–40 bags; the 56-Passenger Motorcoach is the largest unit. Below: seats and day rates for all 8 executive vehicles, per-golfer costs and booking. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

Which vehicle fits a Scottsdale golf group, and how many golf bags fit?

Start with an Executive Sprinter: the Executive Black Sprinter and Executive White Sprinter each seat 14 and hold about 30–40 bags, and a bigger group moves to the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) or the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, the largest unit. Fit as many bags as the vehicle allows. The 56-Passenger Motorcoach is the largest unit. Every other vehicle on this page fits as much as possible. Bags on the Executive Black Sprinter ride in the rear compartment, not the cabin. How does a Scottsdale golf day price?

By the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, with nothing charged by the mile or per passenger: a 4-hour morning in the Executive Black Sprinter is $580 at $145 an hour, and an 8-hour day is $1,015, because 8 requested hours earn 1 free hour and bill 7. The clock runs from first pickup to last drop-off, and the run out, the wait through the round and the return all sit inside that window. Free hours are a published ladder, not a promotion: "Free hours as the day gets longer: 7–11 hours earns 1, 12–14 earns 2, 15 or more earns 3" 8% Arizona tax is the only addition. "Tax only — no booking fee, no service charge, no fuel surcharge, and gratuity never added for you" 1 unit prices differently at the short end: the 56-Passenger Motorcoach carries a 5-hour minimum, so a 4-hour booking on it still bills 5 and costs $1,625.

What does a golf day cost per golfer?

Divide the day total by the golfers riding: 8 golfers on a 4-hour morning in the Executive Black Sprinter pay $580 between them, about $73 each, and with every seat filled an 8-hour day runs about $41 a seat in the 56-Passenger Motorcoach and $73 in the Executive White Sprinter, before 8% Arizona tax. Do that arithmetic before choosing the vehicle, because per golfer the ranking inverts. The Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) costs more by the hour than the Executive Black Sprinter — $225 an hour against $145 an hour — but seats 29 rather than 14, so a full day with every seat taken lands near $54 a golfer instead of $73. Among the 8 executive vehicles priced here, a foursome costs least in the Executive Black Sprinter or Executive White Sprinter: a foursome fits in the Executive Black Sprinter's 14 seats with room to spare, and its 4-hour total of $580 is about $145 each — under the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter at $780.

How do early tee times and pickups work?

Work backward from the arrival time the course itself asks for and book the hours from the first pickup to the last drop-off, remembering that the 4-hour minimum carried by 7 of the 8 executive units is usually the floor an early round is quoted against. Scottsdale Sprinters publishes no drive-time formula, so the desk builds from the arrival target the course gave you plus the pickup addresses and loading order, and puts one pickup time on the confirmation. "Put a street address on the reservation rather than a landmark, and give us the mobile number of whoever is actually meeting the vehicle. Your chauffeur photographs the interior before every trip for our records, so tell them straight away if anything is wrong when you board." Several hotel pickups cost more of the booked window than one: each needs an approach, a legal loading spot, a head count and club handling. Whether the vehicle waits through the round or leaves and returns also changes the quote, so settle that before the date.

Can one booking cover golf and a night out?

Split it into 2 bookings: the round and the ride back belong on the executive units priced above, while a bachelor night in Old Town is a celebration booking on its own page — a different cabin, and a headcount that no longer has to leave room for golf bags. The two halves want opposite things from a vehicle: a golf morning wants forward-facing seats and a rear compartment the clubs disappear into, a night out wants standing room. So this page quotes the golf half, and the Scottsdale bachelor party transportation page quotes the night half.

How do corporate and tournament golf outings work?

As one coordinated movement rather than several separate bookings, because past 56 seats a single vehicle runs out and a second vehicle on the same reservation crosses the large-group line (20+ passengers or 2+ vehicles) that governs both the cancellation window and the written movement plan. Two published lines cover most of what an organiser asks for. "Several vehicles on one booking, coordinated to one schedule with one point of contact" And ahead of the date: "A written movement plan before the date — vehicle by vehicle, pickup by pickup" Group players by when they actually leave, not by title: a first wave and a hospitality wave are two loading times. The larger units are where the per-golfer arithmetic pays. The Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) seats 29 at $1,575 for an 8-hour day — about $54 a seat when full — and the 56-Passenger Motorcoach seats 56 at $2,275, about $41 a seat.

Can one booking cover more than one course in a day?

Yes, as one hourly charter with every stop listed on the reservation: an 8-hour day that takes in 2 rounds bills 7 hours in the Executive Black Sprinter — $1,015 before tax — because hourly bookings carry no per-stop charge at all, however many bag drops the day needs. The only per-stop charge Scottsdale Sprinters publishes sits on a point-to-point transfer, at $50 each; an hourly charter absorbs the second bag drop inside the window already booked. A transfer is still the right product for a group that needs only the two end legs. It is priced as a trip with no hourly minimum: flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off; longer transfers priced from the drive with the empty return included — $295 one way in the Executive Black Sprinter.

What can the group bring on board?

Clubs, bags and drinks ride with the group and food does not, which is the one house rule this page has to flag, while bags load into the rear compartment on the Executive Black Sprinter rather than into its 14-seat cabin, and those Sprinters hold about 30–40 bags. The published rule is "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." On the vehicle itself: "Luggage loads into the rear compartment on this Sprinter, so a full cabin and a full load of bags can travel together. Tell us about oversized or awkward items before the day and we confirm the fit in writing." Flag hard travel cases and boxed gear before the day; they decide the fit. A round starting at the airport stacks passengers, clubs and suitcases into one vehicle: "Count bags, not just seats. Say up front if the group is carrying golf travel bags, ski bags or boxed gear, because those decide the vehicle more often than the headcount does." Two more house lines matter on a long day — "Bottled water on board, the one complimentary amenity on every ride" and "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

How do you book Scottsdale golf transportation?

Send the date, the hours, the golfer count, the bag count and every address, and the desk returns a written quote against today's published rates, held by a 50% deposit on a card that is charged the balance 48 hours before pickup. Golfers and bags are separate questions for a reason: four players with hard-shell travel cases plus airport luggage is a different fit from four with carry bags. "A professional chauffeur on every vehicle, background- and MVR-checked" Cancellation follows the published large-group policy once a movement carries 20 or more passengers or takes 2 or more vehicles: a full refund 30 or more days out, the deposit kept between 14 and 30 days, nothing refunded inside 14. Request a current quote, or call (623) 986-6339.

Things to know

  • Can you store golf clubs on the sprinter van? — Golf-bag capacity varies by vehicle and passenger count. Share the exact number of players, club bags, and other luggage so the team can confirm fit.
  • How much does golf transportation cost in Scottsdale? — Golf pricing depends on the vehicle, passenger and club capacity, pickup route, wait time, and whether the plan continues to dinner or nightlife.
  • Which golf courses do you serve? — Submit the exact course, tee time, passenger count, and club-bag count. Route feasibility and vehicle fit are reviewed before transportation is confirmed in writing.
  • Can you combine golf with other activities? — Many groups connect golf with dinner, Topgolf, or nightlife. The final route is built around the confirmed tee time and venue reservations.
  • Do you offer spring training transportation? — A confirmed Cactus League game can be added to a golf request. Guests purchase tickets directly, then send the stadium, start time, course, and tee time for transportation review.
  • Why do you need the exact course name, not just the golf club? — Some Scottsdale-area facilities have more than one course. Experience Scottsdale’s golf guide distinguishes TPC Scottsdale Stadium and Champions, Troon North Monument and Pinnacle, and Grayhawk Talon and Raptor. Send the exact course, tee time, and property-supplied loading instructions so the route can be reviewed without assuming the wrong entrance or schedule.
